summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86 down 0.28% while the Dow finished at 53,417.16 up 0.26%, extending Monday's Dow versus Nasdaq divergence into a second session as technology refused to lead and defensive money stayed put. The 10 year yield held at 4.70 down 0.72% and Bitcoin crossed and held above 80,000, settling at 80,053.03 up 1.35%, with crypto outperforming every major equity index on the day. Gold pulled back slightly to 4,680.10 down 0.17% after recent strength, crude oil dropped to 84.52 down 1.07% as the Bessent Treasury buyback plan and Iran sanctions dominated the energy narrative, and the VIX barely moved at 15.81. The biggest single stock story was the broad AI cloud and quantum cohort getting hit again, with RGTI down 8.6%, IONQ down 8.5%, DDOG down 4.2%, NET down 4.4%, and MDB down 6.5%, while consumer names like COST up 2.5% and MO up 3.6% picked up the slack. Overseas markets were mostly green with Nikkei at 65,856.43 up 0.49%, Korea at 6,742.74 up 0.68%, and Germany at 26,167.63 up 0.19%, suggesting the US tech rotation is not yet infecting global sentiment. The week's critical events are Wednesday Core PCE and preliminary GDP, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision, so the next 72 hours will set the rate path narrative for September.
